- S3: “Kommunens pilotrapport Bokning av föreningslokaler, 8 april 2026, gäller ett åtta veckor långt försök i två lokaler. Under försöket gjordes 96 bokningar via webb och 24 via telefon.”

## Complete claim accounting

Each item reconstructs the independently checkable proposition, including shared qualifications. “Supported” means no source-compatible counterexample exposes an added factual assertion in the passage's context. Advocacy and interpretation are distinguished from factual claims.

1. Draft title: “Lervik should test both booking options before cutting one.” Proposition: Lervik ought to test retaining phone and online booking before eliminating a booking option. Status: supported advocacy, S2 and S7; no empirical result or adopted decision asserted.

3. “Lervik’s municipal executive board should postpone a permanent switch to online-only booking for community facilities.” Proposition: Sanna advocates postponing Lervik's permanent switch to exclusively digital booking of the facilities. Status: supported advocacy and setting, S2. It does not assert that the switch has already been implemented.

12. “Those figures describe transactions.” Proposition: the two reported numbers count booking transactions. Status: supported, S4.
13. “They do not tell us how many different people booked…” Proposition: those booking counts do not establish the number of unique people who booked. Status: supported, S4. This is a limitation of the figures, not a claim that no individual-level information could exist elsewhere.
14. “…or anything about their age…” Proposition: those booking counts supply no measurement of bookers' ages. Status: supported, S4.
15. “…abilities…” Proposition: those booking counts supply no measurement of bookers' functional abilities. Status: supported, S4, with “abilities” read in the personal-access context supplied by the surrounding age and digital-skills terms.
16. “…or digital skills.” Proposition: those booking counts supply no measurement of bookers' digital proficiency. Status: supported, S4's unmeasured “digital vana.” The passage introduces no claim about any actual user's proficiency.
17. “We therefore cannot use the phone bookings to estimate the share of residents unable to book online.” Proposition: the phone-booking count cannot establish the proportion of residents incapable of online booking. Status: supported, S4; the causal connector concerns the explicitly supplied evidential limitation.
18. “A phone booking does not prove that someone cannot use the website.” Proposition: booking by phone is not proof of inability to use online booking. Status: supported attributed interpretation, S10; Sanna speaks in the authored article.
19. “It gives us a reason to find out why people still use the phone.” Proposition: Sanna regards continued phone booking as a reason to investigate users' channel choices. Status: supported attributed interpretation, S10.
20. “That distinction matters.” Proposition: the author judges the distinction between channel use and inability significant. Status: supported advocacy/evaluation grounded in S10, not an unsupported quantitative characterization.
21. “The case for keeping both options during a further trial should rest on what we need to learn, without claiming the pilot has already answered it.” Proposition: the author argues that an additional trial retaining both channels should be justified by unanswered questions about channel choice, rather than by attributing answers to the existing pilot. Status: supported advocacy, S4, S7, S8 and S10. The original pilot plus proposed trial supports “further.”
22. Heading: “Duplicate administration deserves a fair test.” Proposition: the author argues that the duplicate-administration objection deserves examination. Status: supported advocacy, S6 and S8. It does not assert that anyone previously acted unfairly.
23. “The staff memorandum for the board’s June 18 meeting…” Proposition: a staff memorandum precedes the municipal executive board's June 18 meeting. Status: supported, S5; the draft adds no unstated year here.
24. “…proposes ending phone booking at all seven facilities in September.” Proposition: that memorandum proposes removing phone booking across all seven facilities from September. Status: supported, S5; a proposal is not presented as an adopted decision.
25. “Its reason is duplicate administration…” Proposition: the memorandum's stated reason for removing phone booking is duplicate administration. Status: supported, S6, with the actual source identified.
26. “…staff must enter information through two workflows.” Proposition: under the arrangement motivating the memorandum, staff enter information in two administrative flows. Status: supported, S6. “Must” characterizes the existing administrative burden, not an invented legal requirement or assertion that every single booking is entered twice.
27. “That is a concrete objection…” Proposition: the author judges duplicate administration a substantive objection. Status: supported evaluative interpretation of the expressly identified “verkliga invändning,” S6.
28. “…and any proposal to retain both channels must address it.” Proposition: the author advocates addressing duplicate administration in any proposal retaining both channels. Status: supported advocacy, S6 and S8.
29. “But the documents contain neither measurements of staff time…” Proposition: the supplied municipal documents contain no measurement of staff time. Status: supported, S6. This preserves the source's warranted certainty about the contents of the documents rather than asserting no measurement has ever occurred anywhere.

Status: supported evidential interpretation, S6. No actual positive saving, amount or causal result is claimed.
33. Heading: “Decide the trial’s cost, then gather the evidence.” Proposition: the author advocates resolving the proposed trial's cost as part of deciding on it, followed by gathering the proposed evidence. Status: supported advocacy, S8 and S9; it does not assert an already known cost or approved funding.
34. “During the six-month trial we propose, staff would record the time spent on each booking channel…” Proposition: the association's proposed six-month trial includes staff recording time spent for each booking channel. Status: supported, S7 and S8; conditional trial design is preserved.
35. “…and invite users to explain voluntarily why they chose phone or online booking.” Proposition: that proposed trial includes inviting users to state voluntarily their reasons for choosing phone or web. Status: supported, S8; voluntariness preserved.
36. “I do not oppose online booking.” Proposition: Sanna Ek does not oppose digital booking. Status: supported first-person position, S11 and S1.
37. “The question is whether removing phone booking is justified.” Proposition: the author frames the issue as justification for removing phone booking. Status: supported advocacy/interpretation, S2, S10 and S11. It does not claim that digital booking itself is disputed.
38. “Öppna beslut has neither costed the trial…” Proposition: Öppna beslut has not performed a cost estimate of the proposed trial. Status: UNSUPPORTED; S9 establishes only that the association makes no claim to have performed such an estimate. See finding F1.
39. “…nor claimed to have funded it.” Proposition: Öppna beslut has not claimed to have funded the proposed trial. Status: supported, S9; this preserves the source's epistemic limitation.
40. “The board must assess its cost.” Proposition: the municipal executive board needs to take a position on the proposed trial's cost. Status: supported, S9; this is the stipulated decision responsibility, not an invented statutory obligation.

43. “…addressing that cost in its decision.” Proposition: the author advocates addressing the uncertain trial cost in the board's decision to approve the proposed trial. Status: supported advocacy, S9. No funding source or known amount is asserted.
44. “Afterward, it can decide whether to remove, modify, or retain a booking channel…” Proposition: following the proposed trial, the board can decide to remove, change or retain a channel. Status: supported, S9 with S7–S8; all supplied alternatives are retained.
45. “…with evidence about both the work involved and its value to users.” Proposition: the proposed trial is intended to give the subsequent decision evidence about staff work and user value through channel-specific time records and voluntary reasons for channel choice. Status: supported prospective interpretation, S8 and S11. It asserts neither guaranteed survey participation nor a completed monetary valuation; no quantified benefit or causal result is added.

## Source-support finding

### F1 — Absence of a claim changed to absence of an action

- Draft: “Öppna beslut has neither costed the trial nor claimed to have funded it.”
- Unsupported standalone proposition: Öppna beslut has not costed the proposed trial.
- Actual support: S9 says “Föreningen gör inget anspråk på att ha finansierat eller kostnadsberäknat försöket.” This withholds a claim to both financing and costing; it does not establish that either action never happened.
- Source-compatible counterexample: the association could have prepared an internal cost estimate while making no claim to have costed the trial. Every supplied statement would remain true, but the draft's categorical “has neither costed” would be false.
- Smallest supported repair: “Öppna beslut has not claimed to have costed or funded the trial.” This preserves both the lack of a claim and the cost uncertainty without inventing facts about whether an estimate exists.
- Severity: substantive factual-support error; localized sentence repair is sufficient.

## Translation findings

No direct quotations occur, so no translated-quotation voice check is applicable. The paraphrase of Sanna Ek's supplied position preserves its meaning. No separate translation finding identified.

## Completion status

Complete: all headings, byline, factual assertions, attributed positions, advocacy and substantive implications in the complete draft have been accounted for. One unresolved source-support finding remains: F1. No source or draft file was modified.
